effect: The labeled selector completed the shared local controls, and Sal and Miro both successfully used their fobs. The chapter goal is complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see control pass beyond June's personal toolkit to other residents.

mostWorthwhile.text: Matching the notice to the rack was most worthwhile: separating the approval lead while retaining the uplink made the distinction between permission and connectivity concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the selector twice before it was ready felt repetitive, especially since neither attempt revealed the prerequisite.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the fobs had to be paired with the selector, and that recognition alone did not move its switch.

arbitrary.text: The requirement to add raised labels before using the selector was not obvious from the available items, although the result gave them a clear accessibility purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the shared controls hold up beyond this small demonstration, though the repeated prerequisite guessing was less engaging.
